item.title: KeyCached - Support
item.description:
KeyCached keeps your frequently used snippets a tap away — save the text you paste all the time, then drop it into any app from a custom keyboard, without retyping it. Everything stays on your device.

Need help? Email bspears-dev.handiwork967@passmail.com.

Getting started

  1. Open KeyCached and add the snippets you use often.
  2. Enable the keyboard: Settings → General → Keyboard → Keyboards → Add New Keyboard… and choose KeyCached.
  3. In any app, tap the globe/🌐 key to switch to the KeyCached keyboard, then tap a snippet to insert it.

FAQ

Does KeyCached need “Full Access”? No — inserting your saved snippets works without Full Access. If a specific feature needs it, the app will tell you why before you enable it.

item.title: NoteCached Privacy Policy
item.description:
NoteCached is a private notes app. This policy explains what data is collected, stored, and shared — which is almost nothing.

What We Collect

Nothing.

NoteCached has no account system, no login, no analytics, and no telemetry. No data is ever transmitted to us or any third party. NoteCached cannot comply with legal requests for your data because we never have access to it.

Your Notes

All notes are stored locally on your device and encrypted before being saved to disk. The encryption key is tied to your device and is never shared with anyone, including Apple or us.

Frequently Asked Questions

I forgot my passcode. How do I get back in?

There is no passcode recovery. NoteCached has no account and no server — there is no “forgot passcode” flow by design. If you enabled auto-destruct, 5 failed attempts will wipe the vault. If you did not enable a PIN, you can unlock with Face ID or Touch ID.

item.title: Read Forge - Privacy
item.description:
Read Forge is built to read text, not to collect it. The short version: Read Forge collects no data about you. None leaves your device to me or to anyone else.

Data collection

Read Forge has no accounts, no analytics, no advertising, and no tracking of any kind. The app does not collect, transmit, sell, or share any personal information or usage data.

Your reading content

Text you paste, files you import, and articles you share into Read Forge are stored only on your device. Your library and reading positions never leave it. Deleting the app deletes all of this data.

item.title: DNS Forge - Support
item.description:
DNS Forge helps you set up encrypted, private DNS (DoH / DoT), scope it to specific networks, import and export configuration profiles, and verify it all with built-in diagnostics.

Need help? Email bspears-dev.handiwork967@passmail.com below for what to include.

Getting started

  1. Open DNS Forge and tap a preset (Cloudflare, Quad9, AdGuard, OISD, …) or tap + to add your own resolver or import a profile.
  2. iOS installs the DNS configuration, then you must turn it on: Settings → General → VPN, DNS & Device Management → DNS, and select your profile.
  3. Back in DNS Forge, the status header should show Profile Active and DNS Reachable. Use DNS Resolver Test to confirm which resolver is answering.

Frequently asked questions

How do I add my NextDNS / AdGuard / ControlD account?

Tap + → DNS over HTTPS (or DoT) and paste your provider URL, e.g. https://dns.nextdns.io/<your-id>. Server IP addresses are optional for DoH/DoT — leave them blank and the app will resolve the server name normally. Tap Test Endpoint to confirm it works, then Save.

item.title: Decoding VPNs
item.description:
🔒 VPNs: What They Really Do (And What They Don’t)

VPNs are everywhere these days. Ads, YouTubers, even non-tech-savvy folks are asking if they need one. Here’s the truth: VPNs are tools, not magic shields. They help with privacy, but they don’t make you invisible online.

🛠 How VPNs Work

A VPN (Virtual Private Network) creates a secure, encrypted tunnel between your device and a VPN server. All your internet traffic passes through it, so outsiders like ISPs or public Wi-Fi networks can’t easily see what you’re doing.

item.title: The Normalization of Spyware
item.description:
Protecting Your Privacy in a Digital World

In today’s digital world, our privacy is under threat more than ever. Spyware — often hidden inside popular software — is becoming normalized. Most people don’t read terms and conditions, and even fewer check privacy policies to see how their data is used, analyzed, or stored.

Take Windows, for example. Every update adds new features, which often means more data collection. Microsoft says it’s for system improvement, but it frequently goes further than most realize — collecting everything from basic diagnostics to detailed monitoring of your digital activity. New features like Microsoft Recall take this even further, literally capturing screenshots of your display while tracking usage patterns and device activity across applications. Opting out isn’t straightforward, and these features run quietly in the background.

item.title: Search Engines with Privacy!
item.description: Discovering what someone is searching for on the web can reveal a lot of information about them… Whether it be about their medical issues, financial situation, personal issues, or simply anything that comes to their mind, it will be searched, and in most cases, it will be documented by someone. There are companies out there that are making insane amounts of revenue from data collected from unsuspecting people. For example, Google has stated that they track things that you type into the search bar even if you don’t press “Enter.” Your searches are literally mined, tracked, and packaged up for advertisements to be displayed on web pages you visit. Just last year, Google made 95.38 billion dollars from ad revenue. While this can help bring you better search results when you need to find something useful, I believe that it can be dangerous to have that much information on someone and recommend using an alternative search solution that won’t trade your inquiries to the highest bidder. DuckDuckGo proxies Bing search results, Startpage proxies Google, and Brave is independent - meaning they index their own results from the web. I believe these are all you really need.
